children: Travel booking platform ixigo reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 63.42 crore for the September quarter, compared with a loss of Rs 3.46 crore a year earlier, helped by a partial stake sale in Freshbus and rapid growth in hotel bookings.

Revenue from operations rose 13 per cent year-on-year to Rs 320.96 crore in the second quarter of FY27, from Rs 284.23 crore in the corresponding period last year, according to a regulatory filing by Le Travenues Technology, which operates ixigo.
Total expenses increased to Rs 309.51 crore from Rs 291.89 crore a year earlier.
The company reported quarterly gross transaction value (GTV) of Rs 5,304 crore, up 22 per cent year-on-year, reflecting continued growth in its travel booking business.

Hotels was ixigo's fastest-growing business segment by GTV, with the metric rising 159 per cent year-on-year to Rs 111.34 crore. The September quarter marked the first time the company reported hotels as a separate business line.

In a joint statement, ixigo Group Chief Executive Officer Aloke Bajpai, Group Co-CEO Rajnish Kumar and Group Chief Financial Officer Saurabh Devendra Singh said the company had recorded its highest-ever quarterly profit after tax, aided by the partial sale of its stake in Freshbus.
The executives said the company would continue investing in hotels and artificial intelligence as key drivers of its long-term growth.
